note: Domain C, AboutModal i18n. Seven criteria pre-registered at d4b97fb, before this commit existed, and re-derived here rather than accepted from the report.  METHOD. The Implementer claims the Hebrew was extracted programmatically rather than retyped. That is a claim about process and is not verifiable after the fact, so it was not the thing checked. What was checked is the OUTCOME, which is what the claim exists to protect: the ordered sequence of rendered Text children was reconstructed from the PRE-change TSX (applying the JSX whitespace-collapse rule to the multi-line literals) and from the POST-change TSX resolved against he.ts, and the two sequences compared string by string. 19 visible strings, 19 visible strings, all 19 byte-identical, including the multi-line missionBody/communityBody/attributionBody/sourcesLine that JSX collapses, and including the version template, which resolves to the same rendered string as the old literal plus {VERSION}. accessibilityLabel likewise resolves to the identical string.  THE PROBE WAS FIRED, NOT READ. A mutant of the comparison script was run with exactly one codepoint changed in he.sourcesLine (gershayim U+05F4 -> ASCII quote U+0022 — the same class of one-codepoint loss that cost this repo a real certification today). It reported FAIL, named index 85, and printed both codepoints. Pass and fail cases differ, so the comparison discriminates; a probe whose pass and fail agree has stopped measuring.  CRITERION 2 (trap codepoints) is subsumed by the above and adds nothing: a full byte-for-byte sequence comparison is strictly stronger than counting U+05F4/U+00B7/U+2014/ U+2011 occurrences. Counts were run anyway and agree (2/3/3/1 both sides), plus negative controls for the substitutes an eyeball would miss: U+05F3 geresh 0/0, ASCII quote 0/0, ASCII hyphen 0/0.  CRITERION 4 (the five reused home.* keys) established two independent ways. First, the five pre-change literals are byte-identical to the home.* values they now resolve through, compared as strings not read by eye. Second, and stronger: all five locale files have ZERO deleted lines in this commit (git show --numstat: 23/23/23/20/23 additions, 0 deletions each), so no pre-existing value could have been altered — a silent copy change is structurally impossible here, not merely absent.  CRITERION 6 (lint -21) verified per-file across two detached worktrees, one at this commit and one at its parent, not by trusting a net total. Result: exactly ONE file changed, AboutModal.tsx 21 -> 0, no offsetting movement in any of the other 41 files. Correcting the commit message on a point that happens not to matter: 712 -> 691 is the TOTAL eslint warning count for src/, not the no-hebrew-literal count, which is 654 -> 633. Both deltas are -21, so the conclusion holds, but only because no other rule moved in this commit.  CRITERION 3 (real translations, not pasted Hebrew) — this is the one nothing else catches, since TypeScript checks key presence and not value language. Zero Hebrew letters in the about block of en/es/ru/fr. The single key byte-identical to Hebrew in all four is osmLinkText, which is the ODbL credit string and is Latin in every locale including he. Key-set parity 17/17/17/17/17. Zero Hebrew letters remain in the post-change TSX.  CRITERION 7 verified from the commit itself, self-contained, in a detached worktree created with git worktree add --detach <path> 771f4767d37dec96c8fe9acf3002dc4113d1bbd6 — the commit under review, not its parent with the changed files laid over it. npm run verify clean: 22 suites / 313 tests passed, eslint 0 errors 691 warnings, data:validate dataset OK with every baseline counter unchanged (=).  RTL RULING (the judgement call the Architect referred, and it does not survive contact). The proposition put to me was that C converted a harmless writingDirection: rtl hardcode into a live bug in four locales, because those blocks used to hold Hebrew and now hold English/Spanish/Russian/French. It is false as stated, in two directions.   (1) styles.link holds the ODbL credit, which is Latin text and is byte-identical in all       five locales both before and after this commit. Its content did not change. Half the       alleged defect is pre-existing in the strictest sense.   (2) The LTR-text-under-forced-rtl condition already exists at the PARENT commit, outside       AboutModal and untouched by C: ErrorBoundary.tsx renders {t.errorBoundary.title} and       {t.errorBoundary.body} — fully localised, LTR in four locales — under two       writingDirection: rtl styles. ElulSegulaScreen carries three more. C did not create       this condition; it extended an existing one by one Text node (bodyMuted). So the fix at the proposed scope would close 1 of 8 live instances while producing the signal that the issue is handled — the false-completeness failure this repo has now hit repeatedly. The correct fix is to delete the hardcode and let LanguageContext drive direction, which it already does (document.documentElement.dir on web, I18nManager.forceRTL on native), and that is a theme/shared-component change with no render instrument available to either agent. IN SCOPE as a finding, OUT OF SCOPE as a fix inside this commit — not because a constraint says so, but because at the scope proposed it is wrong and at the scope required it is unverifiable here. Recorded for the owner. Note also src/theme/typography.ts puts writingDirection: rtl on all five shared text styles; it is exported from theme/index and has zero consumers, so it is dead today and would become an eighth-through-twelfth instance the moment anyone used it.  STATED LIMIT, not discovered later. No visual render check was performed by anyone: this is headless. Every criterion above is a textual or structural identity, and the he locale is therefore certified byte-identical while the four LTR locales are certified only as being their own language with the right keys. Whether they LOOK right is unestablished, and the RTL finding lives precisely in that gap.
